judged_text: cook returns raw unfiltered for cook_method raw_html, and the RSS path (Jobs::PollFeed → TopicEmbed.import) never passes content through readability's tag whitelist — that whitelist exists only in import_remote — so third-party feed HTML is stored as cooked with zero sanitization. A malicious or MITM-compromised feed (open() happily fetches plain http) stores <script>/<iframe>/onerror payloads that render verbatim via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb and in normal Discourse topic views — stored XSS executing on the Discourse origin and every embedding page with viewers' sessions; spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb even asserts cooked == raw, codifying the unsanitized behavior as accepted without any security sign-off.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `raw_html` cook mode that bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` now `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), and `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds arbitrary RSS item HTML (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) into `TopicEmbed.import` without any sanitization/whitelist step (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). The embed view renders it verbatim via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). This means third-party feed HTML is persisted and rendered as-is, enabling stored XSS if the feed contains scripts/event handlers/unsafe tags. The spec also codifies this behavior (`post.cooked.should == post.raw`).
